subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Jamie Chen <jamie.chen@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Rate limits & overage pricing - post-demo follow-up

Hi Marissa / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo earlier - good conversation. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can finalize budgeting:

- Estimated monthly token volume (inference tokens, not training): 100M - 300M tokens/month.
- Typical daily pattern: steady baseline ~6M tokens/day with organic spikes during campaigns up to ~15M tokens/day for 1-2 hours.
- Target unit economics: Acme is looking to land at roughly $15 - $20 / 1M tokens (we know this is aggressive; want to understand tradeoffs).
- Bursts: we need to support short burst windows (up to ~10-15K requests/min) without sustained throttling.

Ask: Can you confirm how rate limits and overage pricing would work for a profile like this? Specifically:
1) Burst tolerance (how much above quota can we burst and for how long before 429s?),
2) Options to increase quota temporarily/quickly for campaign windows,
3) Overage unit price (what would we pay per 1M tokens above committed quota?), and
4) If committing to a monthly reserved amount, what discounts / target $/1M can we expect?

I attached our rough usage estimates (acme-usage-estimates.xlsx). Looking to finalize internal budget by 11/12; any timelines on getting a formal pricing/overage proposal would help.

Thanks,
Jamie
Head of ML, Acme AI

Attachment: acme-usage-estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet with daily/hourly token projections)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Chen <jamie.chen@acme.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing - post-demo follow-up

Hi Jamie - great talking yesterday, appreciate the clear numbers. Quick answers and proposed next steps below (I quoted your questions inline).

On the questions you raised:

> 1) Burst tolerance (how much above quota can we burst and for how long before 429s?)
We have two levers: reserved quota and short-term burst allowance. For hosted customers we typically allow short bursts up to ~2-3x of provisioned throughput for ~30-60s before rate limit enforcement (429) begins, depending on model and sequence lengths. For campaign-style bursts we recommend a temporary quota bump (see #2).

> 2) Options to increase quota temporarily/quickly for campaign windows
You can do either: (a) a committed monthly reserve that we scale for you (fastest, predictable), or (b) a temporary one-off quota increase; temporary increases can be enabled within 24-48 hours for most accounts if capacity is available. For mission-critical launches we can pre-approve a burst buffer.

> 3) Overage unit price (what would we pay per 1M tokens above committed quota?)
For reference, our standard hosted overage band for high-volume customers is typically in the $22-30 / 1M tokens range; dedicated/reserved commits can materially reduce that. I want to avoid promising a finalized number over email - Rafael (cc'd) will provide exact proposal numbers based on the commit level.

> 4) If committing to a monthly reserved amount, what discounts / target $/1M can we expect?
With a modest reserved commit (e.g., 250M tokens/mo) we can get to the mid-to-high teens $/1M token range; larger multi-month commitments push that lower. Rafael will lay out tiered pricing options in a short proposal.

Next steps (proposed):
- Rafael to send a 1-page pricing proposal with 2 commit scenarios + associated overage rates (by 11/02).
- Camila to confirm technical rate-limit details and recommended config for your traffic pattern.
- Marissa (me) to share the standard overage and SLA terms and a quick checklist for procurement.

I attached our standard pricing sheet for context (redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf). If that timeline works we can have a pricing/contract draft in-hand before your internal budget review.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference - marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (pricing bands + overage terms summary)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing - technical notes for Acme

Marissa / Rafael - dropping in a couple technical notes for Jamie's team so they can validate against their infra: 

- Burst behavior: our runtime allows transient bursts up to ~3x sustained RPS for short windows (30-60s). Longer bursts will trigger token-based throttling (429) once sustained beyond the buffer.
- Autoscaling / quota: for hosted customers we can configure autoscale policies tied to rolling 1-min / 5-min windows; recommend a pre-authorized temporary bump for campaign days to avoid manual approvals.
- Cost mitigation: prefix/KV caching and response-length caps (max_tokens) can reduce billable tokens by 15-40% depending on prompt reuse; recommend identifying high-reuse prompts to exploit caching.
- Measurement: we'll provide token-level telemetry and a per-route breakdown so Acme can forecast spend during test campaigns.

Suggested config for Acme's pattern:
- Provision baseline for 100M tokens/mo reserve.
- Pre-authorize a temporary quota increase to cover an additional 200M tokens for campaign days (auto-enabled up to 48h before start).
- Enable per-route token caps (50-150 tokens) + caching on FAQ/short-reply endpoints.

I'll prepare a short sizing note and the exact rate-limit numbers for the proposed commit levels and share by EOD 11/01.

- Camila
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sally Ortiz <sally.ortiz@acme.ai>
